items.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe. Utica, New York, November 6, 2010 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: But sometimes he really has an opinion about it, it’s like, “I like that.” “No, the other one’s better.” Sometimes he will actually say what he likes.

ctx.x: Who says, “Well I like take 1, and he likes take 2.”

Mat is pretty cool. Mat is very cool. He is so laid back. He’s like oh it all sounds good to me. He’s pretty much that. You know what I mean? But sometimes he really has an opinion about it, it’s like, “I like that.” “No, the other one’s better.” Sometimes he will actually say what he likes. It’s generally up to the band leader on those sessions. So often I’m hearing on a bass solo like oh, I hope they don’t keep this track. But they’ll say keep this track, and I’m not the leader, I have to — because it’s a time…

can say listen I need to overdub these bars and I know I was nowhere near it. So that’s another good thing in the studio I think is to be aware of it in terms of — because that might be the take they pick.
